What is new here

Our own students. Our own instrument. Our own afternoon.

New data
103 students, collected by us in three days.
New instrument
Six situations, each rated twice.
New comparison
A paragraph against a scale. Nobody had run it.
New assumption broken
Asking directly made people say less.
Every number you are about to see is ours. Nobody had it before this project.

What they feelStyle, fear of judgement, loneliness
What they doClose friends, conversations, avoidance

Three predictions, made before we looked
H1
Insecure students feel lonelier and hold fewer close friends.
Held
H2

Did not hold

Did not hold

What it means

A paragraph wins

because people match themselves to a whole picture, not a checklist.

The scales missed

because people who avoid closeness often don't know that they do.

We thought a good question gets an answer. The opposite happened.
And the students who worried us most reported the least distress.
Honest limits half from one department more men than women one focus group of nine one moment in time, so no causes
Conclusion

A paragraph people recognised themselves in predicted their friendships. Two scales did not.
